title: Implement canary and A/B eval gates for model/config rollouts with automatic rollback
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Purpose: Add tightly-coupled eval gates to canary and A/B rollouts so any model/config change that causes a measurable quality regression is automatically detected and traffic is moved back to the stable variant. This reduces manual rollback toil and prevents bad model pushes from reaching more than a small percentage of traffic.

Background: We currently have manual canary rollouts (10% traffic) and offline evals per PR, but there is no automated gate in the serving/control plane that uses production prompt-set evals and telemetry to block or rollback a rollout. PM/Console teams want a developer-friendly canary flow that guarantees no >1% absolute drop in key eval metrics during canary window.

Acceptance criteria:
- New rollout API supports attaching an eval-suite (prompt set + metrics) to a rollout config.
- During canary/A-B window, system computes eval metrics in production on sampled traffic and from synthetic prompt-set runs.
- Configurable thresholds per metric (absolute and relative) that, if exceeded, trigger an automated rollback to the pinned stable model.
- Rollback is executed via routing policy change with a recordable audit event and an alert to Slack + PagerDuty.
- Dashboards (Grafana) and a Console view show canary metrics, evaluation diffs, and decision timeline.
- Thorough e2e tests and a runbook for handling false positives.

Design/Implementation plan:
1) Eval-suite binding: extend rollout spec to include a reference to an eval-suite id (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-evals, docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Canary+Eval+Suites).
2) Data plane: implement a lightweight in-prod sampler that copies 1% of canary requests (masked/sanitized) to the eval-runner and to synthetic prompt runner. This runs in the serving runtime border to avoid latency impact.
3) Metric computation: standardize metric set (QA-F1, hallucination-rate, answer-coherency-score, latency-p95) and provide functions to compute baseline vs canary deltas. Baseline computed from pinned model over the same traffic window.
4) Decision engine: create a stateless decision service that ingests metrics and applies rules (thresholds, hysteresis, minimum sample sizes). Supports immediate rollback and a 'defer' mode for manual review.
5) Rollback mechanism: routing-layer API to revert to previous model version (runtime route pinning + traffic shift to 100% stable). Persist audit event and trigger notifications.
6) Console/observability: add per-rollout page showing eval diffs, CI/PR links, and a timeline with the rollback link. Grafana dashboard with alerts wired to PagerDuty.

Thresholds and heuristics (initial defaults):
- Minimum samples: 1,000 evaluated responses across canary window.
- QA-F1: absolute drop > 1.5 points OR relative drop > 3% => auto-rollback.
- Hallucination-rate: absolute increase > 2% OR relative increase > 25% => auto-rollback.
- Latency-p95: increase > 100ms absolute => mark as performance regression (alerts, does not auto-rollback by default).
- Hysteresis: require thresholds to be exceeded for at least 2 consecutive evaluation windows (window=10 minutes) unless the regression is extreme (QA-F1 drop > 5 points) then immediate rollback.

Telemetry and privacy notes:
- Sampled request payloads must be redacted per PII policies; ensure KMS-backed masking keys and audit logs.
- All eval results are stored in the evals service with retention 90 days by default (configurable per customer for Private deployments).

Safety and false positives:
- Provide 'defer' mode that throttles automatic rollback and opens a review ticket; useful for low-sample endpoints or high-variance metrics.
- Add a quick manual override in Console to force rollback or resume rollout.
- Post-rollback analysis job to surface top failing prompt examples and suggested action items (prompt engineering, quantization profile rollback, or kernel changes).

Operational runbook (summary):
- PagerDuty page triggered when auto-rollback occurs. On-call follows checklist: verify metric delta, inspect sampled prompts, confirm rollback successful, create incident note, and schedule follow-up remediation with model owner.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How tight should default thresholds be? Conservative defaults reduce customer exposure but increase false positives. We chose conservative initial thresholds and will iterate.
- Sampling cost vs signal: sampling more traffic improves sensitivity but increases cost and storage. Start with 1% sampler, tune per workload.
- Secret handling for sampled payloads in hosted vs private instances; need different retention policies.

Related artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Canary+and+A-B+Eval+Gates
- Prototype PR (eval-runner + decision service): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892
- Grafana dashboard proto: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary-evals

Next steps:
- Finish decision engine prototype (ENG-3143) and integrate with rollout API (ENG-3144).
- Run a staged experiment on non-critical tenants for 2 weeks, collect false-positive/negative rates, then widen rollout.
- Align with PM and Console for final UX copy and alert channels.
comments: 2026-02-16 Marcus Li: Initial scoping meeting with PM and Console. Consensus: attach eval-suite to rollout spec, must support both synthetic prompt-sets and sampled production traffic.
2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Prototype decision engine can evaluate 10 metrics in <500ms across aggregated window; attached PR created (see links).
2026-03-02 Sofia Gomez (SRE): Raised concern about PII in sampled requests. Added masking requirement and KMS integration to design doc.
2026-03-05 Evan Brooks (PM): Requested 'defer' mode and clearer console prompts to avoid noisy automatic rollbacks for early adopters.
2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Implemented rollback API and end-to-end test that simulates a QA-F1 regression and validates traffic re-routing. Preparing for internal dogfood run next week.
